units.name: Anna Kos

tier.basis: In skirmish and multiplayer a hero reaches the field only through a reserve, and KING Art's DevBlog #40 has Anna and Wojtek arrive with Reserve 1, which a player may call in once they own a Barracks or a Workshop (DevBlog #27). That is the tier map's Reserve I gate, t1. The Headquarters named in her wiki infobox is only where reserves are called from and where fallen heroes come back, so it is not her gate. Each player brings one hero, picked with the faction before the match.

cost_band.basis: Her wiki infobox price, counted as iron plus three times the oil, comes to a little over a third of the anchor line mechs' price, under the low threshold. It has stood since September 2020, and no KING Art post read up to DevBlog #47 changes it. She is called in with Reserve I rather than built, and since DevBlog #35 a reserve's price depends on the units it holds; her population cost is left out.

mobility.notes: Her infobox speed equals the rifle squads', the registry's speed reference, and the wiki says she can outpace almost every mech. Like other infantry she hops over low walls and fences, and DevBlog #24 notes that the bear does too. Strafe is the on-foot default.

body.notes: Two bodies come with the one purchase: Anna, a young soldier on foot, and Wojtek, a huge brown bear with a health pool of his own who stays at her side. The game moves the bear like infantry (he vaults walls as soldiers do, DevBlog #24), so nothing here codes him as a bigger body. The body plan describes Anna; the bear is the beast it cannot also hold (see fit_notes).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: her infobox gives Unarmored, which the armour map reads as unarmoured. No source gives Wojtek an armour class; KING Art's posts give him his own health, cut twice (Change Log #17, DevBlog #40). Fallen heroes follow the registry's game-wide rule: at zero health she drops unconscious instead of dying and is out of play, so no enemy can target or finish her, and no source shows her crawling or moving while down. Any friendly infantry squad or hero on foot, an ally's included, brings her round where she lies at no cost, and the Headquarters can also return her. Her four veterancy ranks raise her health (Change Log #04 trimmed those bonuses); cover and lying flat help her as they help every soldier.

sensors.notes: No source gives sight figures for Iron Harvest units (registry), so the band is the medium proposal; the wiki's Pros praise her field of view only in words. No source gives her radar, a detector or stealth. Since DevBlog #35 an unconscious hero lights up less of the map around her.

armament.name: Sniper Rifle
armament.summary: A scoped bolt-action rifle that fires one heavy round every few seconds. Each hit is hard on soldiers, and anyone it fails to kill is thrown to the ground for a moment, open to the next blow. Against armour it does only a fifth to two-fifths as much (Change Log #17 cut its damage to light armour), and buildings take little more. It reaches a good deal further than the registry's reference rifle, the longest reach among the infantry heroes by the wiki's account.

armament.name: Ferocious Maul (Wojtek's melee)
armament.summary: Wojtek's claws, teeth and bulk at touching distance, a swipe every couple of seconds. The bear charges in by himself once the pair is drawn into a fight, bowling soldiers aside, and stays on his target until it is beaten or Anna calls him back; enemy soldiers then turn on him, which is how he shields her. He hits soldiers harder than armour and buildings harder still; DevBlog #40 cut his damage to infantry. The maul is missing while he waits to return after being killed.

crew.notes: One player is Anna. Wojtek is an AI partner, not a second seat or a squad member: he follows her, joins fights on his own and takes her send and recall orders (abilities), he can be sent off alone, he went on fighting after Anna fell until Change Log #17 weakened him, and when killed he comes back after a wait while she lives on. Like the other infantry heroes she can garrison a building, a game-wide mechanic; DevBlog #41 fixed Wojtek's health changing when she does.

abilities.name: Piercing Shot
abilities.summary: Anna takes a moment to aim, then fires one round that goes through everything on its line, so a squad caught in a row can lose several soldiers at once. It hits soldiers about seven times as hard as her rifle and mechs several times as hard, enough to hurt one shot from behind, and it carries past the rifle's reach, to a little under twice the reference rifle's. A wait of somewhat under a minute follows (medium band). Change Log #20 made it fire more reliably and put it ahead of her other actions. Her wiki infobox lists it in a weapon slot marked as an ability.

abilities.name: Ferocious Maul / Call Wojtek
abilities.summary: One button orders the bear: send him at a chosen enemy to brawl, or call him straight back to Anna when a fight turns too heavy even for him, which also lets her slip away while he holds the enemy's attention. Wojtek is a lasting AI partner: always summoned, fighting by himself whenever the pair is engaged, with health of his own. If he is killed, he can be summoned again only after a long wait (wiki Cons and trivia). Change Log #17 and DevBlog #40 both cut his health, the first because he kept on fighting after Anna went down.

abilities.name: Wojtek (passive heal)
abilities.summary: Wojtek slowly heals friendly infantry close to him, Anna included, at no cost, and walks over to wounded soldiers within reach to tend them. Polania trains no medics, so this is the faction's field healing whenever Anna is on the map. Change Log #20 lets him keep tending friendly soldiers while Anna is crouched behind cover. The two wiki pages differ on whether he treats everyone near him at once or one unit after another, and on whether he heals only out of combat (see uncertain).

on_death.notes: The 3C default for an organic unit. In skirmish and multiplayer she is never removed: she drops unconscious and waits to be revived (armour.models), and the Headquarters can bring a fallen hero back as well (Structure page). Wojtek's own deaths are covered under abilities: he returns after a long wait.

strengths.why: Her rifle is deadly to soldiers, and those it does not kill are knocked to the ground (wiki); DevBlog #40 credits Anna and Wojtek with the edge over most infantry groups of the early game.
Piercing Shot drives one round through every target in a line, so it can thin a squad before it closes in, and it still hurts a mech struck from behind (wiki).
Wojtek heals nearby friendly soldiers for free, the only field healing a Polanian army has, since the faction trains no medics (wiki).
The bear charges in by himself, scatters soldiers and draws the enemy's fire onto himself, so Anna can shoot from behind him or get away (wiki; Wojtek page).
At zero health she drops unconscious instead of dying, where no enemy can finish her, and any friendly soldier can revive her for free (registry note on fallen heroes).

weaknesses.why: Her rifle does little to armour of any weight (wiki Cons), and Change Log #17 cut its damage to light targets further, so mechs leave her little choice but to back away.
Groups of infantry, flamethrowers above all, wear Wojtek down fast, and once killed he takes a long time to return (wiki Cons); KING Art has cut his health twice.
She wears no armour, so fire that gets past the bear hurts her in full; the wiki says that against large numbers or armoured support she can only run.
One hero per player, picked before the match and called in only with Reserve 1 (DevBlog #40).

countered_by.why: Anything armoured, from light mechs and exosuits up, shrugs off her rifle; the wiki rates her close to helpless against armour of any weight.
The Rusviet Kolokol mech, armoured against her rifle, knocks her off her feet with its blasts (wiki Cons).
Flamethrowers burn through Wojtek's health quickly (wiki Cons), and without the bear in front Anna has no shield.

counters.why: Rifle hits that kill or floor soldiers, a round that pierces a whole line and a bear that wades in give the pair the edge over most early infantry groups and the other early-game heroes (DevBlog #40).

combos.why: Friendly squads that fight beside Wojtek are healed by him for free, which a Polanian army otherwise lacks; Change Log #20 keeps his healing going while Anna shelters behind cover.
Reasoned: an anti-armour teammate deals with the mechs her rifle cannot hurt, the threat the wiki says she can only run from.

units.memorable: A teenage sniper and her bear: she picks soldiers off from afar or spears a whole line with one piercing round, while Wojtek brawls up front, soaks the fire and patches up the troops around him.
units.as_player: A cheap T1 hero: you are Anna, a fragile sniper with a long reach, and an AI bear fights at your side. Left mouse fires the scoped rifle, which kills or floors soldiers but barely dents armour; Q lines up Piercing Shot, one round through everything on its line; E sends Wojtek at a target or calls him home, and on his own he heals hurt teammates near him. Mechs are your cue to pull back, and a downed Anna waits for a teammate to pick her up.

sources.title: Wojtek, Iron Harvest Wiki
sources.note: The bear's own page, read through the API: very strong against soldiers and barely slowed by bullets, he charges in unless Anna orders him back, so enemies focus on him while she shoots; his attack-or-return order, and the passive heal that treats one nearby infantry unit at a time out of combat and then looks for the next wounded one.

sources.title: Iron Harvest DevBlog #40 - July 2021, KING Art Games
sources.note: Changelog 23 says that Anna and Wojtek enter with Reserve 1 and that, being strong and versatile, the pair outclasses the rest of the early heroes and most infantry groups then in the field; it cuts Wojtek's health and his damage to infantry while leaving her sniping as strong as before. Read as official text that the pair is strong against infantry (roles step 4) and as the official text that calls her a sniper.

sources.title: Iron Harvest Change Log #17, KING Art Games
sources.note: Cuts Anna's damage to light armour and Wojtek's health, because her damage to armour was judged too high and the bear kept going even once Anna had been knocked out.

sources.title: Iron Harvest Change Log #20, KING Art Games
sources.note: Piercing Shot is made more reliable and put ahead of whatever else she is doing, and Wojtek keeps healing friendly soldiers while Anna sits behind cover.

uncertain.note: Reserve I rests on DevBlog #40 alone. Reserve I's condition (a Barracks or a Workshop) comes from DevBlog #27 (https://kingart-games.com/article/81, read, not cited), and no later post read changes it. A hero is unique, and that availability starts at t2 (atypical).

Raw is the infobox's iron plus three times its oil, entered on 22 September 2020; no KING Art post read, DevBlog #20 to DevBlog #47 (articles 67 to 123), changes Anna's price. No page says what that figure buys: she is called in with a reserve, whose price since DevBlog #35 (https://kingart-games.com/article/107, read, not cited) depends on what it holds and stays cheaper than building the units, and heroes also cost reserve coins at the pick (patch 0.11.5, https://kingart-games.com/article/85, read, not cited).

Anti-infantry rests on reading DevBlog #40's line, that the pair's strength and versatility beat most infantry groups of the early game, as official text that the unit is strong against infantry (roles step 4). No post gives her a bracketed label, and the wiki's unit type (Infantry Support Hero, Sniper Hero in September 2020) and opening line are the wiki's own words. Read otherwise, step 4 finds nothing (the registry finds no bonus in per-class damage figures) and step 5 gives assault: the rifle is no tool, and her pace equals the rifle squads', so she is not fast enough for raider.

Support ranks at step 1: Change Log #20 says the bear now heals friendly infantry when Anna takes cover, and its word 'heals' is read as a word form of the alias healer, the way harasses names harasser. Read more strictly, the heal is a passive, which is no button, mode or weapon, so no step would rank it and support would drop out. Disabler ranks at step 3 on the rifle's stun trait, which rests on one sentence of the wiki. Marksman is left out (fit_notes): DevBlog #40 calls her a sniper, which would put it first, but the role needs a sniper weapon of long reach and her rifle is medium. Scout fails its requires (medium speed and sight, no sensor trait or stealth), although the wiki names scouting among her specialities and the Unit page (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Unit, read, not cited) calls the infantry heroes great scouts; those are the wiki's words.
Banded from the infobox reach, entered in September 2020: about 1.4 times the registry's reference rifle, so medium, short of long's edge at 1.5. No KING Art post read changes her rifle's reach.

Stun rests on the wiki's Weapons section, which says soldiers who live through her hit end up on the ground, exposed; no source gives how long. Knockdowns of this kind come from other heavy hits too (the wiki's Cons have the Kolokol knock Anna down, and DevBlog #40's Changelog 23 makes retreating infantry immune to tumbling), so this may be a general reaction of soldiers to big hits rather than a property of her rifle; without it the rifle has no trait and disabler drops out of roles.secondary.
Structures rest on the infobox's building damage figure; the sniper family leaves them out (atypical). No source says the rifle can attack aircraft, so no air target is listed.

The wiki infobox still gives the rifle's damage to light armour from before Change Log #17, which cut it by a third; the summary follows the post. The infobox's other damage figures date from September 2020, and no later post read changes them.
No source says how the round travels; hitscan is the sniper family's default. No damage map exists for the game, so the damage is the family default, kinetic.

The maul is coded as the unit's secondary weapon because the bear is always with her and fights whenever the pair is engaged; it is missing while he waits to respawn. Its figures come from the infobox's second slot. Its knockback rests on the wiki's line that he sends soldiers flying out of his way.

No source gives a figure for the order's cooldown or for Wojtek's respawn wait: the wiki's Cons call it long, and its trivia says only that a wait must pass before she can call him back. The Wojtek page rates him much tougher than Anna, while the posts' health figures for him (cut twice, to well under her infobox health) suggest the opposite. DevBlog #41 (https://kingart-games.com/article/117, read, not cited) fixed his health changing when Anna enters a garrison.

The Anna Kos page says Wojtek treats every soldier near him over time and goes looking for hurt ones within reach; the Wojtek page says he heals one nearby infantry unit at a time, outside combat, and then looks for the next. Change Log #20 has his healing carry on while Anna shelters behind cover. The pattern and kind are the same either way.
Medium rests on the infobox's cooldown for the Piercing Shot slot, which the wiki's Pros repeat; the figure dates from September 2020 and no post read changes it.

Downed-revive follows the registry's game-wide note on fallen heroes; Anna's own pages do not describe her downed state. DevBlog #35 (https://kingart-games.com/article/107, read, not cited) lets infantry and foot heroes revive allied heroes who have fallen unconscious; the Admiral Mason page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Admiral_Mason, read, not cited) says that, unlike him, every other hero is brought round at no cost once a friendly unit reaches them; patch 0.11.2 (https://kingart-games.com/article/83, read, not cited) treats unconscious units as out of play; the Structure page (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Structure, read, not cited) lets the Headquarters bring fallen heroes back.

The 3C proposal default is kept because the downed state is coded as the armour model and no source shows a hero being removed for good in skirmish or multiplayer. If the unconscious body that teammates can revive counted as an outcome of its own, no on-death term would fit: wreck is barred for organic units.

Two, for Anna and the bear, who has his own health and is always summoned; he is not a squad member (see crew). If a companion is not counted as a body, the count would be left out. DevBlog #24 (https://kingart-games.com/article/77, read, not cited) says the bear vaults low walls the way soldiers do, the one hint read on how the game moves him.

Infantry: KING Art calls Anna, Olga and Gunter the infantry heroes (Change Log #04, https://kingart-games.com/article/92, read, not cited) and lists Anna Kos with the infantry whose cover response it improved (Change Log #08, https://kingart-games.com/article/96, read, not cited).

The Kolokol link names the unit the wiki's Cons single out; its id follows the DevBlog short name. Massed infantry are left out of countered_by: the wiki says she stands little chance against large numbers, but DevBlog #40 has the pair beat most infantry groups.
Reasoned from the wiki's Cons (hopeless against armour) and its general description (she can only flee from armoured support); no source names this pairing.

fit_notes.note: KING Art calls her a sniper (DevBlog #40) and every source builds her around a scoped rifle, but marksman needs a sniper weapon that reaches long or further, and hers reaches about 1.4 times the reference rifle, medium. Her long-reaching shot is the Piercing Shot ability, which the role rules do not read as a weapon.

The wiki names scouting among her specialities and praises her long field of view, and its Unit page calls the infantry heroes great scouts, but scout's requires fail: she moves at the rifle squads' pace, no source gives a sight figure, and she has no sensor trait, stealth, mark or reveal. Those are the wiki's words, so step 1 of roles.secondary does not read them either.

fit_notes.wanted: command-companion: a lasting AI partner, usually an animal, that fights beside you on its own and takes short orders such as attack or come back
fit_notes.note: Wojtek is a permanent second body with his own health that charges into fights by himself, takes send and recall orders, shields Anna by drawing fire and respawns after a long wait when killed. launch-drones is for expendable minions released on a key, so it does not fit. reinforce-squad's respawning-followers variant matches only the bear's return after a wait once he is killed, not a partner who fights by himself and obeys orders, and Change Log #17 has him fighting on after Anna fell, so it is not linked; the merge pass may want it beside the new pattern.

fit_notes.wanted: a soldier with an animal partner (a humanoid body plus a beast)
fit_notes.note: One body plan holds one shape: Anna is a humanoid, while Wojtek, the second body of the purchase, is a large bear that the beast plan would describe. The pair shows only in body.count and body.notes.

atypical.note: A named hero, one per player, who enters with Reserve 1 (DevBlog #40), the tier map's t1 gate; our unique availability starts at t2, as the registry note expects for heroes called in with Reserve I.

The auto-target mount is our proposal for Wojtek's maul: the bear picks his own targets while the player aims Anna's rifle. The humanoid plan describes Anna, who carries no such mount; the break comes from a companion's attack sitting on a soldier's unit.
Her rifle's infobox gives it damage against buildings, a little more than against mechs, while our sniper family leaves structures out.
The rifle throws surviving soldiers to the ground for a moment (wiki), coded as stun; she is a t1 hero, and our stun starts at t2.

units.name: PZM-13 "Mocny"

tier.basis: Built at the Advanced Polanian Workshop, by the wiki's infobox; the basic Polanian Workshop builds only the Rycerz, the Strażnik and the Śmiały. One upgrade beyond the basic buildings is the tier map's Advanced Workshop gate. DevBlog #35 (February 2021) let a reserve hold it for two reserve coins, but the reserve is a side-wide call-in, not its gate.

cost_band.basis: Changelog 26 in DevBlog #45 (June 2022) cut its oil price, and its iron price is the one DevBlog #43 (December 2021) set; the wiki's infobox shows both since June 2022, and no later post read changes them. Counted as iron plus three times the oil, it lands a little under the medium threshold, at about four fifths of the line-mech anchor and a little below the Łowca. Its population cost is a cap, not a price, so it is left out.

mobility.notes: Walks on four legs at half the pace of the rifle squads, the game's speed reference, and turns even more slowly, so its own page calls it easy to rush and to outflank. Iron Harvest has no tanks: it is a little quicker than the Łowca, Polania's line mech, keeps about the Wotan's pace, is slower than the Knox, and outpaces both other factions' artillery mechs, the Erlkönig and the Nakovalnya. Handling stays pivot, the many-legs default: it is no small walker, and no source gives a reason to change it. Planted it cannot move at all (deploy-anchor). As a medium mech it breaks through small buildings as well as light cover: game-wide terrain breaking, not the crush trait.

body.notes: Four legs carry an asymmetric body: a large cabin with view ports and a small machine-gun turret on the right, and on the left a huge cannon, longer than the body that carries it, fixed facing forward. Planting turns the front legs into spikes driven into the ground, and the gun tilts upward; the body plan stays the same. Spider frame by the Iron Harvest notes' interim reading for walkers on many legs whose main gun is fixed facing forward (night decision of 27 October 2026): the fixed gun shows in the cannon's body-aim mount (see uncertain and fit_notes). Large: a medium mech and a self-propelled gun, both large in our size examples.

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: the infobox's Medium maps to heavy through the armour map. By the Armor page, that class shrugs off most light weapons but is easy prey for field cannons and anti-mech mechs. Its own page calls it frail for a mech of its class, with little health even at the top rank, though better plated than the lightly armoured Saxon and Rusviet artillery mechs. Directional: hits on a mech's weak rear do about twice the damage (Armor page), and Change Log #06 (October 2020) fixed a bug that had spared the Polanian and Rusviet artillery mechs that extra damage; its page still says it has no rear weakness (see uncertain). Veterancy adds health and base repair is game-wide; neither changes the class.

sensors.notes: No source gives sight figures for Iron Harvest units (the registry's sight reference), so the band is the medium proposal. No source gives it radar, a detector or stealth. Planted, its shells ignore line of sight, but nothing read says it fires beyond its own sight or needs a spotter.

armament.name: Cannon (Mobile)
armament.summary: The big cannon held level for direct fire while the Mocny walks. It points only where the body faces, so the slow-turning mech swings round to aim it, and it fires one shell at a time with a long pause between shots. It reaches about three quarters further than the reference rifle. By the infobox it hits the game's Light armour class hardest, then the Medium and Heavy classes, infantry a little less and buildings about half as hard as light mechs, and each shell bursts over a small area. The wiki calls the walking Mocny a mobile anti-mech unit that can stand up to lighter mechs; DevBlog #30 (September 2020) and Changelog 26 (DevBlog #45) raised its damage against armour.

armament.name: Cannon (Siege)
armament.condition: Only while planted in siege mode, which the Deploy order sets up; it replaces the mobile cannon until the Mocny packs up again.
armament.summary: Planted, the Mocny tilts the same cannon upward and lobs its shells over obstacles, ignoring line of sight. It reaches nearly three times as far as the reference rifle, but it cannot hit anything inside a dead zone close in, a little under half the reference rifle's reach, and it covers only a narrow cone ahead. A direct hit lands a little softer than the mobile shell, but the blast around it is far stronger, several times so against mechs, so static or slow targets such as dug-in infantry, buildings and heavy mechs suffer most; moving units can get clear before a shell lands. Changelog 24 (DevBlog #41, September 2021) roughly halved its reload and raised its damage against the Medium and Heavy classes, and Changelog 26 (DevBlog #45) raised it again against infantry and Medium armour.

armament.name: Machine Gun
armament.summary: A machine gun in a small turret on the right of the cabin, covering only about the right-hand half of the circle. Its bursts hurt infantry and do next to nothing to any armour or to buildings, and it reaches a little short of the reference rifle: close-in defence against soldiers, not a second main gun.

crew.notes: No player seats: RTS units are ordered, not driven. The cabin with its view ports implies a crew, and the walker class makes it a crewed machine. Solo by decision 2A: no source says the side machine gun fires at the same moment as the cannon, so the two count as firing one at a time and both stay with the driver. It has no passenger seats.

abilities.name: Deploy
abilities.summary: Plants the Mocny: the front legs become spikes driven into the ground and the cannon tilts up for indirect fire (the siege cannon, armament/1, in place of the mobile one), reaching further and hitting harder, at the cost of a dead zone close in and a narrow cone ahead. It cannot move while planted, and each change of mode takes a while, during which it is open to attack; ordering it again packs it up. No source gives a cooldown or how long the change takes.

abilities.name: Smokescreen
abilities.summary: Walking mode only. Puts up a smoke screen at the Mocny that blocks line of sight, cover for itself and for friendly units nearby. The wiki says it surrounds the mech and works while it walks; Changelog 24 (DevBlog #41, September 2021) made the Mocny's screen static, so it now stays where it was laid instead of moving with the unit, and made smokescreens smaller and shorter-lived in general. Its page says the cooldown runs out about when the smoke clears; no figure is given.

abilities.name: Smoke Canister
abilities.summary: Siege mode only. Lobs a smoke shell at a chosen spot within reach, and a fixed smoke screen that blocks line of sight forms where it lands, to cover friendly units or the Mocny itself. Changelog 24 shrank and shortened every smokescreen. No cooldown figure is given.

modes.name: Siege mode (deployed)
modes.summary: Planted on its spiked front legs: it cannot move, and the cannon tilts up to lob shells (armament/1) in place of the mobile cannon, with a longer reach, a far stronger blast, a dead zone close in and a narrow cone ahead. The Smoke Canister takes the Smokescreen's place. Nothing read says the machine gun falls silent or that its armour changes.

on_death.notes: Like every destroyed mech it leaves a wreck that nearly any infantry squad can recycle for a little iron and oil, the same small haul whatever mech it was (Recycling Wrecks page); allies share it. Another mech or exosuit stepping on the wreck, or an explosion such as an artillery strike, removes it first, and wrecks give infantry no cover. No source says its destruction harms anything nearby.

strengths.why: Two guns in one walker: it fights on the move with direct fire, then plants to lob longer, harder-hitting shells, so its page ranks it the most adaptable of Iron Harvest's medium mechs and artillery pieces.
Long reach on the move and longer still once planted, where its shells arc over obstacles and pay no heed to line of sight.
Smoke in both modes: a screen laid where it stands while walking, and a canister lobbed onto a chosen spot once planted, to hide itself or friendly units.
Its shells hurt every armour class, better against armour all round than the Erlkönig's, so the walking Mocny doubles as a mech hunter.
Better plated than the lightly armoured Saxon and Rusviet artillery mechs, so on the move it can trade blows with lighter mechs.

weaknesses.why: It walks and turns very slowly, so rushers and flankers reach it easily, even before it plants.
The cannon is fixed facing forward, so the slow-turning mech must swing round to aim, and a unit that gets behind it has time to work before it can answer.
Planted, it cannot fire at anything close in and covers only a narrow cone ahead, so units inside its dead zone or off to the sides are safe from the cannon.
Changing mode takes a while and leaves it open to attack, and once planted it cannot move; units on the move can step out of the way of its slow-landing shells.
Fragile for a medium mech: its health stays low even at the top rank, so it goes down quickly once it draws fire.

countered_by.why: Anything at the rifle squads' pace or faster, twice its speed, can rush it, slip into its dead zone or round its fixed gun to the flank, and dodge its planted shells.
Field cannons and anti-mech mechs are what its Medium armour class is weak to (Armor page), and its page calls it frail for a mech of that class.

counters.why: Planted, its long shells pound buildings, which cannot move out of the blast.
Soldiers dug in at one spot cannot dodge its planted shells, whose blast covers an area, and the side machine gun keeps infantry off it up close.
Heavy and mega mechs are too slow to leave the impact zone, so its planted shells hit them hard, and on the move its cannon still hurts armour well.

combos.why: Its page says it does best tucked behind other units or with good support while it shells from range: a sturdy frontline keeps away the rushers and flankers it cannot handle.

units.memorable: Polania's two-mode artillery walker: it fires a forward-fixed cannon on the move, then spikes its front legs into the ground to lob long shells over cover, hiding itself and friends in smoke.
units.as_player: A mid-tier walking gun with two jobs. Walking, left mouse fires a forward-fixed cannon, a slow, heavy shot that hurts mechs, aimed by turning the whole sluggish walker; a side machine gun guards your right and a smoke key hides you. Deploy to plant: you cannot move, and the cannon lobs long shells over cover into a narrow cone with a blind zone close in, while a second smoke key lobs a screen onto a spot. Keep a frontline ahead: whatever reaches your flank or dead zone wins.

units.name: Sd. KS 49 "Grimbart"

tier.basis: Built at the basic Saxon Workshop with no upgrade, by the wiki's infobox (the Advanced Saxon Workshop builds it too), and Change Log #20 (March 2021) counts it among the light, tier 1 mechs. DevBlog #35 (February 2021) lets it be picked only for the second reserve, Reserve II, where it costs one reserve coin; the reserve is a side-wide call-in, so the production gate decides the tier.

cost_band.basis: Changelog 25 in DevBlog #43 (December 2021) cut its iron and oil price to what the wiki's infobox shows, and no later post read changes it. Counted as iron plus three times the oil, it sits a little above the low band's lowest price, at about half the line-mech anchor. Its population cost is a cap, not a price, so it is left out.

mobility.notes: Walks on very short legs at about half the pace of the rifle squads, the game's speed reference, and turns slowly, so faster units outrun and outmanoeuvre it and it reacts poorly to attacks from several sides (its page). Iron Harvest has no tanks: it keeps the pace of the Wotan, Saxony's line mech, is a little quicker than the Łowca, and is far slower than the Strażnik and the Isegrim, the light and medium mechs it is compared with. Handling stays pivot, the two-legs default: it is no small walker. Like other light mechs it breaks through small amounts of cover, game-wide terrain breaking, not the crush trait. The Sweep roots it while it fires.

body.notes: A heavily armoured box that bullets cannot pierce, set on stubby legs, with a thin arm on each side: a large rotary gun on the right and a pinching claw on the left. Its body is much bigger than that of the Strażnik, its Polanian counterpart. Humanoid mech: a two-legged mech with a torso and arms (see uncertain on the legs). Medium: a light mech, and light walkers are medium in our size examples, though a bulky one. No source uses the claw as a weapon: the gun is its sole armament.

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: the infobox's Light maps to medium through the armour map. Its page calls it the most durable of the light-armoured mechs: even massed rifle squads hardly dent it, while field cannons and anti-mech units hurt it badly. Directional: by the Armor page, hits on a mech's weak rear do about twice the damage, and its own page says it takes extra damage from behind. Change Log #20 (March 2021) raised its health; veterancy adds more and base repair is game-wide, and neither changes the class.

sensors.notes: No source gives sight figures for Iron Harvest units (the registry's sight reference), so the band is the medium proposal. No source gives it radar, a detector or stealth.

armament.name: Gatling Gun
armament.summary: A big rotary gun on the right arm, its only weapon. It fires bursts of bullets, each hitting infantry more than three times as hard as a Strażnik bullet; by the infobox it does a quarter of that to the game's Light armour class, less again to Medium and Heavy, and almost nothing to buildings. It reaches a little further than the reference rifle, enough to outrange the Strażnik slightly. The gun points where the slow-turning mech faces. Since DevBlog #35 (February 2021) its ordinary fire suppresses targets too, which KING Art says makes it better against groups; suppressed infantry move and fire far more slowly.

crew.notes: No player seats: RTS units are ordered, not driven. The walker class makes it a crewed machine, and a KING Art post's caption (DevBlog #15) speaks of a Grimbart pilot. One weapon, so solo. It has no passenger seats.

abilities.name: Sweep
abilities.summary: The Grimbart roots itself and fires without pause across a frontal arc whose width the player sets: the wider the arc, the longer it stays locked in the sweep, firing a far longer burst than an ordinary attack. DevBlog #35 (February 2021) raised the sweep's suppression and its area, so it pins the infantry it rakes harder, while everything in the arc takes the gun's usual damage. Its page counts the rooting among its faults, and the infobox gives it a long wait between uses.

on_death.notes: Like every destroyed mech it leaves a wreck that nearly any infantry squad can recycle for a little iron and oil, the same small haul whatever mech it was (Recycling Wrecks page); allies share it. Another mech or exosuit stepping on the wreck, or an explosion such as an artillery strike, removes it first, and wrecks give infantry no cover. No source says its destruction harms anything nearby.

strengths.why: Its rotary gun mows down infantry by the squad and fares fairly well against light mechs, all the more at elite rank.
The most durable of the light-armoured mechs: even big groups of riflemen hardly dent it, so it can wade into infantry.
Since DevBlog #35 its ordinary fire suppresses too, slowing the movement and fire of the infantry it targets and making it better against groups.
The Sweep rakes a whole arc at once, damaging groups of targets together and pinning the infantry caught in it.
Its gun slightly outranges the Strażnik's, so Polania's light anti-infantry mech cannot easily kite it.

weaknesses.why: Slow to walk and to turn: faster units outrun and outmanoeuvre it, and it struggles to answer attacks from several sides at once.
Its bullets do little to medium or heavy mechs or to buildings, and it has no other weapon to deal with them.
The Sweep roots it until the arc is done, the longer the wider the arc, leaving it a sitting target for the guns that hurt it.
Hits from behind do extra damage, about double by the Armor page, and the slow mech is poorly placed to turn and face them.

countered_by.why: Anti-mech units such as the Łowca and field cannons do extra damage to it (its page), and the Armor page names field cannons, gunner squads and anti-mech mechs as the bane of its armour class.
Named on its page among its main dangers: field cannons punch through its armour and outreach its gun.
Named on its page as an anti-mech unit that does it extra damage.
Its page calls it vulnerable to artillery, which its slow pace cannot escape.
Units at the rifle squads' pace or faster, about twice its speed, outrun and outmanoeuvre it and can reach its back, where hits do more.

counters.why: It devastates infantry: even large rifle squads such as the Polanian Riflemen and Rusviet Vanguards do little to its armour while it cuts them down, and its suppression pins the survivors.
Light mechs, the game's Light armour class, often lose to it head-on and one on one, outranged and outgunned by its rotary gun.
Named on both pages: its own page says light mechs like the Strażnik often lose to it one on one, and the Strażnik's page says the Grimbart outranges it slightly and outguns it heavily.

combos.why: Its page wants it used with heavier anti-armour units that handle the mechs, while it deals with infantry and light armour.
The Saxony page's Great Wall formation sets a Grimbart beside a pair of Kaisers, whose cannons duel the enemy mechs while it keeps infantry away.

units.memorable: Saxony's boxy gatling mech: a rotary gun that shreds and pins infantry, and a sweep that roots it to rake a whole arc the player draws.
units.as_player: A cheap, early anti-infantry brawler. Left mouse spins a heavy rotary gun that shreds and suppresses infantry and chips light mechs, aimed by turning your slow, boxy walker. Your key plants you for a sweep: drag out the arc and you rake it with a long burst that pins everyone inside, but the wider the arc, the longer you stand rooted. Anti-mech guns and artillery are your bane, so fight beside teammates who kill mechs and never show the enemy your back.

units.name: SKS 300 "Kaiser"

tier.basis: Built at the Advanced Saxon Workshop, by the wiki's infobox. DevBlog #30 (September 2020) took the three mega mechs, the Kaiser among them, out of the Reserve and made them need an Advanced Barracks on top of an Advanced Workshop. Change Log #04 later dropped the barracks need for campaign and challenge maps only, so skirmish and multiplayer still ask for both, and no later post read changes that. Both advanced buildings together are the tier map's t3 gate.

cost_band.basis: DevBlog #43 (December 2021) set the iron and oil price that the wiki's infobox has shown since January 2022, and no later post read changes it. Counted as iron plus three times the oil, it lands a little above the high threshold and well short of very high: about half again what the anchor line mechs such as the Wotan cost, and the dearest of the mega mechs. Its population cost, among the largest in the game, uses up the cap rather than paying a price, so it is left out.

mobility.notes: Walks on four legs at a little under half the pace of the rifle squads, the game's speed reference, and its own page ranks it among the slowest units of all, easy to flank and outpace. Iron Harvest has no tanks: it is somewhat slower than the Wotan, Saxony's line mech, keeps about the Tur's pace and lags behind the Gulyay-Gorod, the other mega mechs. Handling stays pivot, the many-legs default: it is far too big for the small walkers' strafe, and no source gives another reason to change it. From its first veterancy rank it can entrench, and then it can neither walk nor turn (deploy-anchor). Like the other heaviest mechs it walks straight through brick and stone buildings and flattens cover, sandbags and wire underfoot: game-wide terrain breaking, not the crush trait.

body.notes: A boxy hull plated like a bunker and standing on four legs; the wiki's Saxony page says Saxon mechs often look like conventional tanks on spider or crab legs. The cannon sits on the roof in an armoured housing of its own that looks like a turret but is locked facing forward, so the whole mech turns to aim it, and a machine gun in a ball mount guards each of its four sides. Spider frame, by the Iron Harvest notes for a walker on many legs whose main gun is fixed: the gun locked forward shows in the cannon's body-aim mount, and the tank-like hull only in these notes (see uncertain and fit_notes). Entrenching lifts the cannon housing to bare rocket batteries at the front and on both flanks; the body plan stays the same. Huge: KING Art presented it with the Tur as two of the biggest mechs in the game, and giant mechs are huge in our size examples, although its own page calls it far more compact than the Tur (see uncertain).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps reads the infobox's Heavy as heavy through the armour map; the registry note and check A make the mega mechs super-heavy, and it is huge and tier 3. Its health tops that of every other mega mech and of the Samson, and its page ranks only the Icarus as tougher, shrugging off almost everything short of massed artillery. By the Armor page, heavy armour all but ignores light weapons, so only field cannons and anti-mech weapons do it real harm. Directional: hits on its rear do about twice the damage (Armor page), and its own page says it suffers more from behind, where neither the cannon nor the rockets can answer. Veterancy raises its health by about a third and then by half, and repair at the base is game-wide; neither changes the class.

sensors.notes: No source gives sight figures for Iron Harvest units (the registry's sight reference), so the band is the medium proposal. No source gives it radar, a detector or stealth.

armament.name: Main Cannon
armament.summary: A big gun in the forward-locked roof housing: it fires only where the hull points, so the mech turns to bring it to bear. One heavy shell at a time with a long pause between shots, reaching about three quarters further than the reference rifle. By the infobox it hits the game's Light armour class hardest, Medium a little less and Heavy as hard as infantry, while buildings take half that. Each shell bursts over a small area, but the blast is far weaker than the Tur's, so on its own the gun deals poorly with groups of soft targets. The wiki calls it the Kaiser's main anti-armour firepower and says it lets the mech beat any other mech one on one. While entrenched it can only cover a narrow arc ahead.

armament.name: Side Machine Gun
armament.summary: Four heavy machine guns in ball mounts, one on each side of the hull: between them they watch every direction, and they keep shooting while the mech walks. Each fires long bursts with short pauses and reaches a little less far than the reference rifle. The infobox shows them doing little to any armour and next to nothing to heavy armour or buildings, so they are for infantry and light mechs.

armament.name: Rockets
armament.summary: Three six-tube batteries, one at the front and one on each flank, that the rising cannon housing bares when the Kaiser entrenches; none faces the rear. While it stays dug in, each attack order fires them beside the cannon and machine guns: salvos of fifteen small rockets every few seconds, each rocket bursting over an area. By the infobox they hit infantry (the game's Unarmored class, by the Armor page) about three times as hard as the Light and Medium classes and the Heavy class least, with some harm to buildings. They reach about two fifths further than the reference rifle but not as far as the cannon, and the wiki counts their short reach among its faults.

crew.notes: No player seats: RTS units are ordered, not driven, and no page read names a crew, so the walker class makes it a crewed machine. Driver-gunner: once it has entrenched, its rocket batteries, on mounts of their own at the front and flanks of the hull, fire beside the forward cannon, which keeps shooting into its narrow arc (the Kaiser page says they add firepower). By decision 2A the driver walks the mech, aims the cannon by turning the body and fires the side machine guns, since no source says those fire at the same moment as the cannon; the gunner fires the rockets, which pass to the driver when no gunner is aboard. It has no passenger seats.

abilities.name: Entrench
abilities.summary: Opens once the Kaiser reaches its first veterancy rank (the wiki; patch 0.11.2 let the mega mechs rank up a little faster). The mech plants itself and can neither walk nor turn, and the cannon housing rises to bare the rocket batteries, the entrenched mode's Rockets (armament/2). Dug in, the cannon covers only a narrow arc ahead. Planting takes a moment in which it is exposed, and a planted Kaiser suffers even more from field cannons and artillery. No source gives a cooldown, how long the change takes or how it packs up again.

modes.name: Entrenched
modes.summary: Dug in: it cannot move or turn. The raised cannon housing bares the Rockets (armament/2), batteries that fire only in this mode, to the front and both flanks but not behind; the cannon keeps firing, but only into a narrow arc ahead. Nothing read says the side machine guns fall silent or that its armour changes. The wiki says field cannons and artillery hurt it most in this state.

on_death.notes: Like any destroyed mech it leaves a wreck, which nearly any infantry squad can strip, the way it collects a resource stockpile, for a little iron and oil, the same small haul whatever mech it was (DevBlog #24; Recycling Wrecks page); since Change Log #04 allies get the haul too. Another mech or exosuit stepping on the wreck, an explosion such as an artillery strike, or a death too close to a live mech wipes it out first, and the wreck gives infantry no cover. No source says its destruction harms anything nearby.

strengths.why: Only the Icarus is tougher: its health tops every other mega mech's and the Samson's, and its heavy plating shrugs off small arms, so it can head a formation and soak fire while little but massed artillery wears it down.
Its long-reaching main cannon hits every armour class hard, so it can duel and destroy any other mech one on one, the other mega mechs included.
Machine guns at the front, the back and both flanks keep infantry off it whichever way they come, and they fire while it walks.
Once veteran it can entrench to open rocket batteries that add salvos to its front and both flanks, and a supported pair of dug-in Kaisers makes a line that enemies can hardly break.
As one of the largest mechs it walks straight through brick and stone buildings that stop smaller mechs and over cover, sandbags and wire, so few obstacles block its path.

weaknesses.why: It ranks among the game's slowest units: it cannot chase, and lighter units outmanoeuvre it, flank it and keep out of its reach.
The cannon is locked facing forward, so a target on its flank or behind it is safe from its anti-armour gun until the slow mech turns.
Hits from behind do about double damage, and neither its cannon nor its rockets can fire to the rear, leaving only the rear machine gun to answer there.
Dug in, it cannot walk or turn and its cannon covers only a narrow arc ahead; planting leaves it briefly exposed, and field cannons and artillery hurt it even more while it is planted.
The cannon reloads slowly and its blast is weak, so until its machine guns or rockets are in reach it handles soft targets and groups of light units poorly, worse than the Tur or the Gulyay-Gorod do.
The priciest Saxon unit to build, and its heavy population cost keeps the number in the field small.

countered_by.why: Artillery is the bane of the slow heavy mechs (Unit page), and massed artillery is what the Kaiser page says wears it down, all the more once it digs in and can no longer step out of the fire.

Heavy armour is hurt in earnest only by field cannons and by mechs carrying anti-mech guns (Armor page), and the Kaiser page names enough well-placed field cannons among its main dangers, above all against a planted Kaiser.
Named on the Kaiser page: field cannons in numbers and in good positions grind it down, above all while it is entrenched.
Agile units at rifle-squad pace or faster, more than twice its speed, slip round to its flanks and rear, where the cannon cannot follow and hits do about double, and can lead it on a chase.

counters.why: Its cannon can duel and kill any other mech one on one, the other mega mechs included, and its machine guns also tear into light mechs.
Its four machine guns mow down infantry closing in from any side, even while it walks, and once it digs in its rockets add bursts that hit soldiers hardest.

combos.why: The Kaiser page advises fielding at least two together, and a supported pair dug in makes a nearly unbreakable line, the core of the Saxony page's defensive formation.
It soaks the fire while anti-armour mechs add the damage: its page wants mech destroyers beside it on the attack and lists the Wotan among the Saxon support a defensive pair of Kaisers wants.
The Wotan page says the fragile Wotan does well behind a Kaiser that takes the hits while the Wotans add firepower.
The Kaiser page pairs it with artillery when it goes on the attack, and the Saxony page's formation can add the long-range Erlkönig.
Anti-infantry backup covers its gaps on the attack (Kaiser page), and the Grimbart, an anti-infantry mech, is among the support that its page and the Saxony page's formation give a pair of Kaisers.

units.memorable: Saxony's walking fortress, a bunker on four legs: a forward-locked cannon that out-duels any mech, a machine gun on every side and, once veteran, rockets bared by digging in.
units.as_player: A late, costly walking fortress that leads the push. Left mouse fires the forward-locked cannon, a slow, heavy shot that hurts any armour, so you aim by turning the whole lumbering mech; right mouse sweeps the side machine guns over infantry on any side, even on the move. Once you rank up, the deploy key digs you in: you cannot move or turn and the cannon covers only a narrow cone, while a gunner, or you alone, fires the rockets on your front and flanks. Guard your back, where hits do double.

sources.note: The mech cost rebalance labels the unit Kaiser (Mega Mech), the newest bracketed label, and sets its price in iron and oil, which the wiki's infobox matches; no later post read, up to DevBlog #47, changes it.

uncertain.note: Step 1 finds no role: the newest bracketed label, Mega Mech (DevBlog #43), names none, and neither does DevBlog #24's older Saxony Gunfort heading. No official text read says what it is strong against, and the registry finds no bonus in the game data, so step 4 finds nothing and step 5 gives assault: very slow and super-heavy. The Lore box on its wiki page, which may copy the in-game Codex (the wiki shows the Codex only as a picture), calls it effective against both infantry and mechs; no readable source shows that line in the game, so it is read as the wiki's words, like its italic opening line. Read as official, step 4 would offer anti-infantry and anti-armour with no bonus to rank them, and the line names infantry first.

Anti-armour rests on the Kaiser page's prose calling the cannon its main anti-armour firepower, read as a label that names the weapon by its job (can_target step 3); without it the list would be anti-infantry alone, from the splash cannon and the side machine guns, small arms that do little to mechs. Siege is no candidate: the cannon reaches long but is aimed straight at targets in view, the rockets that entrenching adds reach only medium and are not lobbed, so the mode fails siege's deploy clause, and Entrench, a veteran button that not every copy has, gives nothing at step 2. The rockets count at step 3 as a secondary weapon although only a dug-in veteran fires them; they add only anti-infantry, through their splash, which the other weapons already give. The wiki's Cons call the cannon poor against soft targets, but they are the wiki's words, not official text, so they drop nothing.

The infobox names only the Advanced Saxon Workshop, and the Advanced Saxon Workshop page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Saxon_Workshop) lists the Kaiser among the units it builds; the Advanced Barracks comes from DevBlog #30. Change Log #04 (https://kingart-games.com/article/92) removed that second building for campaign and challenge maps only and says multiplayer and skirmish keep it; no later post read changes it. Both pages read, not cited.

The Kaiser page's Cons still rank it second among the game's dearest units, a line written before DevBlog #43; at the current prices it tops the registry's price check list, ahead of the Tur, the Samson and the Gulyay-Gorod.

The infobox speed was entered on 23 May 2021 by an anonymous edit with no comment, in place of an April 2020 figure a little lower, and no KING Art post read from DevBlog #20 to #47 changes the Kaiser's speed. Either figure is under half the reference pace, so the band holds. The comparisons in mobility.notes use the infobox speeds on the SKS 156 "Wotan", PZM-24 "Tur" and SHM-70 "Gulay-Gorod" pages of the Iron Harvest Wiki (read, not cited).

Deploy-anchor stands for Entrench, which a Kaiser gains only at its first veterancy rank, so an unranked Kaiser cannot deploy. It is kept because the button and its mode are recorded, as on the Red Alert 2 deploy units; mobility traits have no stock-only rule like the one for sensor traits.

Walking through buildings and over cover rests on the Unit page (the heavy and mega mechs pass easily through brick and stone buildings), the Mech page (the biggest mechs trudge through large structures) and the Sandbags page (mechs flatten sandbags by stepping on them), all on the Iron Harvest Wiki, read, not cited; the Kaiser page itself says nothing of buildings.

Coded spider-frame by the Iron Harvest notes' reading for walkers on many legs (night decision of 27 October 2026), until a body tie-break for such walkers is settled at the rule-fix round after R4. In the opening check one coder chose spider-frame and the other casemate. By the casemate or hull-turret tie-break, a main gun locked forward in the hull makes a fixed-gun hull. But casemate is listed only for ground vehicles and hovercraft of medium or large size, so the Kaiser would break three of its rules, as the reconciled entry did before this note. The Saxony Empire page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Saxony_Empire, read, not cited) says Saxon mechs often look like conventional tanks on spider or crab legs. Multi-turret would fit only if the four ball-mounted guns, which the wiki calls machine gun turrets, counted as turrets; the note says they do not.

No source gives its footprint. KING Art's DevBlog #22 (https://kingart-games.com/article/74, read, not cited) introduced it with the Tur as two of the largest mechs in the game and called both huge; the game labels it a Mega Mech (DevBlog #43), and the wiki's Unit page calls the heavy and mega mechs the biggest mechs. Coded huge from the giant mechs of the size examples. Against that, the Kaiser page's trivia calls it much more compact than the Tur; large would follow only if it were judged no bigger than an assault mech.

The armour map alone gives heavy (infobox Heavy); super-heavy comes from the registry note on the mega mechs and from check A for a huge unit at tier 3. The health comparisons in armour.notes and strengths/0 use the infobox figures on the PZM-24 "Tur", SHM-70 "Gulay-Gorod" and ZR-25 "Samson" pages of the Iron Harvest Wiki (read, not cited).

The doubling comes from the Armor page; the Kaiser's own page says only that hits from behind do more. Versions of its page from May and June 2020 said it had no weak spot, until an August 2020 edit added the rear weakness, and no post read settles it, so directional follows the registry's rule for every mech.
No damage map: step 5 keeps the cannon default, armour-piercing, which the wiki's calling it the main anti-armour firepower also gives. If that wording did not count, its blast would give explosive.

Splash rests on the infobox's blast radius, which counts as saying the hit hurts an area. The Kaiser page calls the cannon's splash damage low and says it lacks the splash to handle infantry well, but it never calls the area tiny.

The infobox weapon figures (reach, damage, bursts and pauses) were entered in April 2020, during the backer beta, and no later KING Art post read changes the Kaiser's weapons, so they are read as current. The comparisons use the registry's reference rifle.
No source says how the shell travels; projectile is the cannon family's default. Hitscan for the side machine guns is likewise their family's default.

None of the three weapons lists air targets, the rockets included. The Kaiser page's Pros suggest, with a hedge, that it can even shoot at airships, but they name no weapon, and no other source says which Kaiser weapon reaches aircraft; the Gunship page's claim that every unit can attack it is too broad (registry). The SHM-70 "Gulay-Gorod" page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (read, not cited) says that mech's machine guns fire at flying units, which may hold for the Kaiser's guns too. Structures are listed from the infobox's building damage figures.

Limited-arc: each machine gun sits in a ball mount on one side of the hull, and no source says how far it turns (aim tie-break step 3). By that step the front gun alone would be fixed; the one entry takes the side guns' mount.

Only a Kaiser that has reached its first veterancy rank and dug in fires the batteries, so not every copy has them. They are coded as a secondary weapon of the entrenched mode, as the registry note on the infobox's ability slots now says for the Kaiser's Rockets, and as the slot rule says of a weapon that a mode adds while the main gun keeps firing. Acquired does not fit: it covers a weapon that a rank adds with no ability, and here the rank opens the Entrench button, which enters the mode. Their figures come from the infobox's third weapon slot, the one marked as an ability, entered in April 2020 with the other weapons' figures.

Limited-arc: one battery faces forward and one faces each flank, and the Kaiser page says neither the rockets nor the cannon can fire to the rear (aim tie-break step 3). By that step the front battery alone would be fixed; the one entry takes the flank batteries' mount, as for the side machine guns. The page's Abilities line has entrenching raise its damage output on every side, which is read as the batteries together with the rear machine gun.

Driver-gunner rests on the rockets alone, which fire only for a veteran Kaiser that has dug in. The crew rule leaves out weapons that a mode swaps in and weapons that an upgrade, a passenger or a kill adds, but not one that a mode adds while the main gun keeps firing, and the Kaiser page has the rockets add firepower while the cannon still covers its narrow arc. If a weapon reached only through a veteran button should not count, the proposal would stay solo. The side machine guns stay with the driver because no source says they fire at the same moment as the cannon (the page says only that they fire on the move and cover every side); if they do, they would go to the gunner too.

The unlock at the first rank rests on the Kaiser page's Weapons section and on the Veterancy page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Veterancy, read, not cited), which says the first rank opens each unit's veteran ability; the Tur and Gulay-Gorod pages say the same of their mega-mech abilities. DevBlog #24, from the backer beta, lists the deploy with the unit, apart from the veteran abilities it names, without saying when it opens. Patch 0.11.2 (https://kingart-games.com/article/83, read, not cited) let all three mega mechs reach veterancy a little faster.

The wreck rests on DevBlog #24, which made mech wrecks harvestable, and on the Recycling Wrecks page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Recycling_Wrecks, read, not cited), which says every destroyed mech leaves one and gives who can recycle it and what removes it; Change Log #04 (https://kingart-games.com/article/92, read, not cited) shares the haul with allies. The Kaiser page says nothing of its wreck.

Artillery also rests on the Unit page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Unit, read, not cited), which calls the heavy and mega mechs slow and open to artillery. Field cannons go under anti-armour because the same page says their direct-fire guns pierce even heavy mech armour from far off, while the Kaiser's own page names them beside artillery and once groups them with it. The agile units that kite it are read as units at least as fast as the rifle squads, since its page gives no speed and nearly every unit outpaces it. Whether aircraft beat it is left open, since no source says which of its weapons reach fliers; DevBlog #45 (https://kingart-games.com/article/121, read, not cited) says the game lists the Gunship as effective against heavy armour.

The Kaiser page says it can kill any other mech, and the infantry and carried weapons too, but its Cons call it vulnerable to field cannons and its prose has massed, well-placed field guns wear it down, so the weapon systems stay out of counters and field cannons sit in countered_by.

The Wotan, Erlkönig and Grimbart parts rest on the Saxony Empire page (its Great Wall formation: a pair of Kaisers backed by a Wotan or a Stiefmutter, a Grimbart, sometimes a field cannon, and at times the Erlkönig) and on the SKS 156 "Wotan" page (Wotans do well behind a Kaiser that soaks damage), both on the Iron Harvest Wiki, read, not cited. The Kaiser page itself links the Wotan and the Grimbart among the support a defensive pair wants, and on the attack wants it backed by artillery, by mech destroyers and by units that deal with infantry.

units.researched_by: batch r3, opening check (agents A and B, reconciled)

fit_notes.wanted: a fixed-gun hull for walkers, on many legs and at huge size
fit_notes.note: The main gun is locked forward in an armoured housing on the roof of a boxy, bunker-like hull on four legs. Spider frame (a body on several visible legs) fits the legs, but not the tank-like hull with its fixed gun, which shows only in the cannon's body-aim mount. Our casemate plan has that shape, but it is listed only for wheeled, tracked and hover vehicles of medium or large size.

atypical.note: It walks on four legs at a little under half the rifle squads' pace by its infobox speed, and our many-legs type starts at slow; the Tur and the Wotan, the other heavy Iron Harvest mechs compared in mobility.notes, are very slow too.

units.name: Olga Morozova

tier.basis: In skirmish and multiplayer a hero reaches the field only through a reserve. No source read names Olga's, so Reserve I, the tier map's t1 gate (open once a player owns a Barracks or a Workshop), is the band the evidence best supports: KING Art groups her with Anna and Gunter as the infantry heroes (Change Log #04), and both of those come with the first reserve. The Headquarters is only where reserves are called from. Each player brings one hero, picked with the faction before the match.

cost_band.basis: No source read gives her price: her wiki page carries no figures, and no KING Art post from DevBlog #20 to DevBlog #47 names one. Low is a judgement from the wiki prices of the other heroes who fight on foot or horseback: Anna's is very low, while Gunter's and the cavalry hero Michał Sikorski's are low, as is that of Victor Popov, the Rusviet exosuit hero. Patch 0.11.5 also gave every tier 1 hero the same reserve-coin price at the pick. No raw figure is stored.

mobility.notes: No source gives her speed figure. The wiki says she can outrun regular infantry, which under the speed rules gives the rifle squads' band, medium, since it does not say much faster; the wiki's Unit page also calls the infantry heroes fast in general words. She goes faster still on Changa's back (see modes). Strafe is the on-foot default; transform stands for Ride the Tiger, which switches her into the ridden form.

body.notes: A lone agent on foot. Changa, her Siberian tiger, is not a second body on the field most of the time: she keeps out of sight until Olga calls her to ride or until an attack ends the ride, when the tiger fights on her own for a short while (see abilities and modes).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: the wiki infobox's Unarmored, read through the armour map. The wiki counts her small health and lack of armour among her weaknesses, and patch 0.11.5 and Change Log #06 both lowered her health; on Changa's back she has more health than on foot (Change Log #06). Fallen heroes follow the registry's game-wide rule: at zero health she drops unconscious instead of dying (DevBlog #30 fixed a bug in her animations that stopped her doing so) and is out of play, so no enemy can finish her, and no source shows her moving while down. Any friendly infantry squad or hero on foot, an ally's included, revives her where she lies for free, and the Headquarters can return her too. Her four veterancy ranks raise her health (bonuses trimmed in Change Log #04).

sensors.notes: No Iron Harvest source gives sight figures (registry), so the band is the medium proposal. Her camouflage hides her fully on a passive of its own, so it is coded there as the cloak pattern (abilities), not as the stealth sensor trait. No source gives her radar or a detector, and no unit in the game detects hidden ones (registry).

armament.name: Submachine gun
armament.summary: Her main gun: short-ranged, yet one burst can drop a soldier, so she can wipe out a lone squad (wiki; the Rusviet page says the same of single squads). Up close she also cuts soldiers down with her shashka sabre, the melee blow every infantry unit has (see uncertain). Change Log #04 halved the gun's damage to light armour and raised the sabre's, so the gun now does only a small part of what the blade does to light mechs. She cannot shoot while riding Changa.

crew.notes: One player is Olga. Changa is an AI partner who waits out of sight: she is Olga's mount on call, and she fights on her own for a short while after an attack ends the ride. While riding, Olga still counts as an infantry hero: Change Log #04 lets her be healed at barracks and medic stations without leaving the tiger's back, and medics charge the same as when she is on foot.

abilities.name: Remote Detonators
abilities.summary: Olga fixes a charge to a chosen mech or building. It blows by itself once she has gone far enough away, or she can fire it by hand, so she can set it while hidden and walk off before it goes. It hurts light and medium armour most, heavy armour a little less, and buildings and soldiers least; since DevBlog #41 its damage scales with her veterancy, lower before her first rank and higher at her top two. Patch 0.11.5 had already weakened it. No source gives a cooldown or how many charges she may have out.

abilities.name: Ride the Tiger
abilities.summary: Calls Changa out of hiding and puts Olga on her back: quicker and tougher than on foot, but in plain view, since her camouflage stays off for as long as she rides. Ordering an attack makes her jump down, and the tiger then joins the fight briefly before slipping away (the triggered entry below). She uses it to travel fast or to escape. Change Log #09 fixed Changa coming straight back after being killed: she now waits out her cooldown first.

abilities.name: Ride the Tiger: Changa joins the fight
abilities.summary: When an attack drops Olga off the tiger, Changa stays and fights beside her for a short time, then goes back into hiding. The tiger is a lasting AI partner with health of her own: her claws and teeth hit soldiers hard but mechs barely (Change Log #04), and if she is killed she can be called again only after a cooldown (Change Log #09). The wiki notes that she gives Olga far less active help than Anna's bear or Gunter's wolves give theirs.

abilities.name: Camouflage
abilities.summary: Enemies cannot see Olga while none of them is near. An enemy that gets her within about half its range, or any action of hers, such as using an object, gives her away, and she hides again once no enemy is close; riding Changa keeps it off. Standing still is not needed, only distance. While hidden she is out of play for enemy fire: patch 0.11.2 stopped ground-attack orders from hitting units in stealth mode. The wiki calls her the only base-game unit that could hide this way.

modes.name: Riding Changa
modes.summary: Olga on her tiger's back: faster than on foot and with more health (Change Log #06), but visible, since her camouflage stays off, and unable to shoot, because an attack order makes her jump down and ends the mode. No source gives either form's speed figure, and the wiki's comparison keeps both in the medium band, so the mode records no new mobility. She still counts as infantry for healing (Change Log #04).

on_death.notes: The 3C default for an organic unit. In skirmish and multiplayer she is not removed: she drops unconscious until revived (armour.models), and the Headquarters can bring her back too (Structure page). Changa's deaths are covered under abilities: she can be called again after a cooldown.

strengths.why: Enemies cannot see her until they come close or she acts, and she hides again once they have gone, so she can scout and set charges unseen; the wiki calls her the only unit of the base game that hides actively.
Her remote charges, left on a mech or building and set off by walking away, hit light and medium mechs hardest and grow with her rank (DevBlog #41); the wiki calls her explosives fairly powerful.
One burst of her gun can drop a soldier, and with the sabre up close she can cut a single squad apart (wiki).
Calling Changa gives her a quicker, tougher ridden form for getaways and long trips (wiki; Change Log #06).
At zero health she drops unconscious instead of dying, and any friendly soldier can revive her for free (registry note on fallen heroes).

weaknesses.why: Little health and no armour at all (wiki Cons); KING Art cut her health so that, as an assassin, she has to choose her targets instead of joining any fight (Change Log #06).
Her hiding drops whenever an enemy comes too close, whenever she acts, and for as long as she rides Changa (wiki Cons).
Her gun reaches only a short way, so she must get near what she shoots, which is what gives her hiding away (wiki).
On the tiger she is visible and cannot shoot, and once she drops off, Changa helps only briefly, far less than the other infantry heroes' animals (wiki Cons).
One hero per player, picked before the match and called in through a reserve.

countered_by.why: The wiki names anti-infantry units among her threats: with little health and no armour she loses a straight fight with them.
Massed infantry overwhelm her (wiki Cons): her gun handles one squad at a time, not several at once.

counters.why: A single squad caught alone falls fast to her gun and sabre (wiki; the Rusviet page credits her gun with destroying single squads).
Reasoned: a charge left on a mech while she stays hidden does heavy damage, most of all to light and medium mechs (wiki; DevBlog #41), and the mech cannot shoot at her while she is hidden.
Reasoned: she can creep up to enemy buildings unseen and leave charges on them that go off when she leaves (wiki; DevBlog #41 lists their damage to buildings).

combos.why: Reasoned: unseen near the enemy, she can keep targets in view for artillery, which since Change Log #17 loses any target that drops out of sight.

units.memorable: A Tsarist agent who stays unseen while no enemy is near, leaves charges on mechs that go off once she walks away, and rides her Siberian tiger out of trouble.
units.as_player: A T1 stealth hero: you are invisible until an enemy comes near or you act, and you vanish again once the coast is clear. Left mouse fires a short-range SMG that drops soldiers; Q sticks a charge on a mech or building that blows when you walk away; E calls Changa to ride, faster and tougher but in plain sight, and attacking jumps you off while the tiger fights briefly beside you. Massed infantry and anti-infantry units are your end; a downed Olga waits for a teammate to revive her.
